mitigations.detail: Disable the javascript: URI handler in Internet Explorer Zone settings via GPO (IExplore security zones → Scripting → Active scripting → Disabled for Internet zone).

hypotheses.fpr: url.dll,OpenURL is used by Windows itself for .url shortcut file handling and IE-integrated applications. The key differentiator is the inline javascript: or vbscript: URI scheme (not a file path). Legitimate usage always references a file path, not an inline script. FPR is near-zero for the javascript:/vbscript: pattern.

hypotheses.title: Registry Run Key Set to Binary in Staging or User-Writable Path
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor on Windows is suspected of establishing persistence by writing a registry Run or RunOnce key that points to a malicious binary in a user-writable or staging directory, ensuring execution at the next user logon. Hunt for registry writes to HKCU or HKLM Run keys where the value data points to executables in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, %PUBLIC%, or C:\ProgramData rather than %ProgramFiles% or %SystemRoot%.

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 13 — Run key in staging path
pivots.detail: TargetObject contains (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run OR HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run OR HKLM\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) AND Details contains (\AppData\ OR \Temp\ OR \Users\Public\ OR \ProgramData\) AND Image NOT IN (msiexec.exe, ccmexec.exe)

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 13 — RunOnce key write
pivots.detail: TargetObject contains (CurrentVersion\RunOnce OR CurrentVersion\RunOnceEx) AND Details contains executable extension (.exe, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .vbs) — RunOnce keys with script content in user paths are commonly used by info-stealers and droppers for single-run persistence.

pivots.label: New value from non-installer process
pivots.detail: EID 13 where Image NOT IN (msiexec.exe, setup*.exe, installer*.exe, ccmsetup.exe) AND TargetObject in Run key — persistence set by cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, or an unusual binary has no legitimate explanation outside installer context.

detection_logic.query_hint: EventCode=13 TargetObject=*\CurrentVersion\Run* Details=*(\AppData\|\Temp\|\Users\Public\|\ProgramData\)* Image NOT IN (*msiexec*)

mitigations.name: Restrict Registry Permissions
mitigations.detail: Apply restrictive ACLs to HKLM Run key — allow writes only by SYSTEM and signed installers. HKCU Run cannot be restricted without removing user rights, so focus detection on HKCU and enforce path-based rules.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.detail: WDAC startup enforcement rules can block Run-key-launched binaries that are unsigned or not in %ProgramFiles%. ASR rule 'Block persistence through WMI event subscription' covers related persistence vectors.

refs.label: Red Canary TDR — Registry Run key abuse
CISA AA22-320A — TA453 persistence via Run keys

hypotheses.fpr: Software installers (msiexec.exe, Inno Setup, NSIS) legitimately write Run keys during installation — these always have signed parents and paths under %ProgramFiles%. Microsoft Update and OneDrive write Run keys with paths under %ProgramFiles% or %LocalAppData%\Programs (a known exception to the staging-path rule). Alert on unsigned binary targets in staging paths unconditionally.

hypotheses.title: File Dropped into Windows Startup Folder by Non-Installer Process
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor on Windows is suspected of placing a malicious script or shortcut in the Windows Startup folder to achieve persistence without modifying the registry, ensuring execution at every user logon. Hunt for file creation events in the per-user or all-users Startup directory from any process that is not a signed software installer.

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 11 — file created in Startup folder
pivots.detail: TargetFilename contains (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\ OR C:\Users\*\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\) AND extension IN (.lnk, .bat, .cmd, .vbs, .js, .hta, .exe, .ps1) AND Image NOT IN (msiexec.exe, explorer.exe, ccmexec.exe)

pivots.label: LNK shortcut pointing to staging path
pivots.detail: Sysmon EID 11: .lnk file created in Startup directory, followed by Sysmon EID 23 or a read of the newly-created .lnk. If the LNK TargetPath (readable via file inspection or LNK parser) points to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or a UNC path, it confirms persistence to a remotely staged payload.

pivots.label: Startup folder modification by PowerShell or cmd
pivots.detail: EID 1: powershell.exe or cmd.exe creating a file in the Startup path via Copy-Item, cp, xcopy, or redirect (>). This pattern is used by malware that downloads a payload then installs Startup persistence in a second step.

detection_logic.query_hint: EventCode=11 TargetFilename=*\Startup\* Image NOT IN (*msiexec*,*explorer*,*ccmexec*)

mitigations.name: Restrict File and Directory Permissions
mitigations.detail: Set SACL on Startup folder directories to alert on file writes. Apply WDAC startup enforcement — binaries in Startup folder can be subjected to the same code integrity checks as any other execution path.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.detail: Use WDAC or AppLocker to block execution of script files (.bat, .vbs, .js, .hta, .cmd) from the Startup folder for non-administrative users.

hypotheses.fpr: Software deployment tools (SCCM, Intune, PDQ Deploy) may place shortcuts in the Startup folder as part of managed application deployment. These always have a signed installer parent and the resulting shortcut target is a signed binary in %ProgramFiles%. Alert on script files (.vbs, .bat, .ps1) in Startup folders without restriction — there is no legitimate use case for script-based Startup folder entries outside managed deployment with a change ticket.

hypotheses.title: Anomalous Large Outbound Upload Over Established C2 Beacon
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor who has established a C2 channel is suspected of exfiltrating collected data over the same beacon channel, producing an anomalous spike in outbound data volume to a previously low-volume C2 destination. Hunt for established HTTPS connections with significantly asymmetric upload-to-download ratios (high upload, low download) to external IPs or recently-registered domains that have been communicating in a periodic, low-volume pattern.

pivots.label: Netflow / proxy: upload volume spike
pivots.detail: Same external IP or FQDN that had < 1 KB/hr average outbound suddenly transfers >10 MB in a single session — consistent with staged archive exfiltration over an existing beacon. Filter to connections on port 443 with consistent inter-beacon jitter matching C2 profile.

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 3 — process + byte counts
pivots.detail: Image IN (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, mshta.exe, wscript.exe, known-C2-process) making outbound connection with bytes_sent > 5 MB to an IP with low historical connection count. Non-browser process uploading >5 MB is near-certain exfil.

pivots.label: DNS resolution spike before upload
pivots.detail: >3 DNS queries to the same FQDN within 5 minutes (C2 jitter check-in pattern) followed by a long-lived TCP session on 443 with upload bytes exceeding 5 MB — the pre-exfil beacon check-in pattern seen in Cobalt Strike, Havoc, and Sliver.

detection_logic.query_hint: EventCode=3 Initiated=true Destination NOT IN (known_cdns, trusted_ips) bytes_sent > 5MB Image NOT IN (*chrome*,*msedge*,*onedrive*)

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.detail: Deploy SSL/TLS inspection on the egress proxy to inspect HTTPS content for data-loss indicators. Alert on outbound sessions with upload bytes > 10 MB from non-approved applications.

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.detail: Configure DLP policies on the network egress and endpoint to detect and block outbound transfers of sensitive file types (.xlsx, .docx, .pdf, PII patterns) regardless of the channel.

refs.label: CISA AA23-320A — Scattered Spider data exfiltration
Vectra AI — C2 exfil over HTTPS detection

hypotheses.fpr: Cloud sync clients (OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive) and backup agents produce large uploads routinely. Allowlist by: signed process (OneDrive.exe, Dropbox.exe, backup agent binary), known cloud storage IP ranges, and upload pattern matching sync schedules. Alert on unsigned or unexpected process uploading >5 MB to an external IP not in the approved cloud provider list.

hypotheses.title: Staged Archive Created then Transferred Over C2 or Outbound Channel
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor on Windows is suspected of compressing collected data into an archive before exfiltrating it over an established C2 channel or direct outbound connection, following the classic collect-stage-exfil pattern. Hunt for archive creation events in staging paths followed within minutes by an outbound network connection from the same process or parent chain.

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 11 — archive in staging path
pivots.detail: TargetFilename endswith (.zip OR .7z OR .rar OR .tar OR .gz OR .cab) AND TargetFilename path matches (\Temp\ OR \ProgramData\ OR \Users\Public\ OR \AppData\Roaming\) AND Image NOT IN (winrar.exe, 7zFM.exe, explorer.exe) — automated archiving from cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unknown binary in staging path.

pivots.label: Sysmon EID 3 — outbound within 300s of archive creation
pivots.detail: Correlate: EID 11 archive creation AND within 300s EID 3 outbound TCP to external IP from same HostID AND Image IN (powershell.exe, curl.exe, certutil.exe, bitsadmin.exe, cmd.exe). The tight time window between archive and upload confirms exfil intent.

pivots.label: 7-Zip or WinRAR with password flag in CLI
pivots.detail: Sysmon EID 1: 7z.exe OR rar.exe CommandLine contains (-p OR -hp) — password-protected archive is a red flag for data staging. Combined with output path in a temp/public directory, this is high confidence pre-exfil staging.

detection_logic.query_hint: EventCode=11 TargetFilename=*(\Temp\|\ProgramData\)*.zip | followby EventCode=3 Initiated=true Destination NOT IN (known_ips) within 300s [by host]

mitigations.name: Data Loss Prevention
mitigations.detail: Inspect outbound traffic for compressed archives containing sensitive file types. Block upload of password-protected archives from non-approved applications via DLP policy.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.detail: Monitor egress proxy for large compressed payloads uploaded to cloud storage or direct IPs. Flag sessions where Content-Type indicates archive formats (application/zip, application/x-7z) from non-standard applications.

refs.label: CISA AA23-075A — LockBit data exfil before encryption
DFIR Report — staged archive exfil chain

hypotheses.fpr: Legitimate backup scripts and IT archiving tools create password-protected archives in ProgramData regularly. Allowlist by: signed archiver binary launched by a known backup service account, archive destination matching a backup share path, and scheduled (not interactive) execution context. Alert on interactive user or attacker-linked process creating archives in staging paths followed by outbound transfer.

hypotheses.title: DNS Tunneling Exfiltration via High-Volume Subdomain Queries
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor on a compromised host is suspected of exfiltrating data using DNS tunneling, encoding collected data as subdomain labels in queries to an attacker-controlled domain, using DNS responses as the return channel. Hunt for anomalously high volumes of unique subdomain queries to a single apex domain, particularly where subdomain labels are long, high-entropy, and not resolvable to real resources.

pivots.label: DNS query volume anomaly
pivots.detail: >50 unique FQDN queries to the same apex domain within 60 minutes from a single endpoint, where the subdomains are not repeating (i.e., >40 unique subdomain labels). This pattern matches DNS tunnel data chunking — each query carries ~30–60 bytes of base32/hex-encoded data.

pivots.label: Subdomain label entropy
pivots.detail: Subdomain labels with entropy > 3.5 bits/character and length > 20 characters are characteristic of base32 or hex-encoded payloads. Legitimate CDNs and cloud services use short, readable, or structured subdomain labels.

pivots.label: DNS record types: TXT and NULL queries
pivots.detail: DNS queries for TXT, NULL, or ANY record types to a single domain at high volume (>20 TXT queries/hour) — DNS tunneling tools (dnscat2, iodine) use TXT/NULL records for return data due to higher response size limits versus A records.

detection_logic.query_hint: dns_query rrtype IN (TXT,NULL) | stats count by apex_domain | where count > 50 AND unique_subdomains > 40

mitigations.name: Filter Network Traffic
mitigations.detail: Restrict DNS resolution to an enterprise recursive resolver with RPZ (Response Policy Zones) blocking newly-registered and uncategorised domains. Log all DNS queries and forward to SIEM for volume anomaly detection.

mitigations.name: Network Intrusion Prevention
mitigations.detail: Deploy DNS security solutions (Cisco Umbrella, Infoblox TIDE, Palo Alto DNS Security) that detect high-entropy subdomain patterns, tunnel fingerprints (dnscat2, iodine signatures), and block DNS tunneling at the resolver.

refs.label: CISA — Turla ComRAT DNS exfiltration analysis

hypotheses.fpr: CDN domains (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly) use long randomised subdomain labels for asset addressing — these appear high-entropy but repeat on subsequent queries. Allowlist apex domains in the Alexa/Tranco top 10K. Alert on: apex domains registered <30 days ago, domains not categorised in threat intelligence feeds, and TXT/NULL record volume anomalies to uncategorised domains.
